boot.evidence: Three real boots of the pinned kernel (7.2.0-rc4-g169b17ff3f66) from a private copy of the Debian+docker image: a fresh boot, then two resumes of the same snapshot, each reaching WEB_UP_MARKER with dockerd and the demo container up.

c1_snapshot_records_base.evidence: snapshot stopped the guest cleanly, wrote snapshots/snap-a.cow and a metadata record whose BASE_SIZE equals the backing image (54140a722974..., sha256 recorded); the file-level gate tests/test-snapshot.sh covers GUEST_UNAME and the remaining fields.

c2_resume_restores_filesystem.evidence: A file written in the guest BEFORE the snapshot (/root/snap-a.txt, content verified by its md5 computed on the host and printed by the guest) was readable AFTER up --from: same md5. Both markers are base64 in the typed command, so the console echo cannot fake them.

c2_copy_on_resume_immutable.evidence: The snapshot COW sha256 was identical after both resumes, and a second marker written during resume 1 produced ZERO occurrences of its md5 during resume 2: the second boot did not see the first boot writes. The daemon log confirms the policy: "cow: reusing the header ... (resume semantics)".

c3_list_and_remove.evidence: 'uml4termux snapshots' listed snap-a; 'snapshot --rm snap-a' removed both the COW and the metadata file.

c4_refuse_different_image.evidence: Resuming against a different backing image (a copy, mtime changed) was refused with rc=1 BEFORE any boot: the message names the recorded size/mtime and the observed ones, and no new daemon pid appeared in the registry.

base_image_untouched.evidence: The private copy of the backing image had the same sha256 before and after three boots: guest writes went to the COW (54140a722974... unchanged).

no_leftovers_from_this_run.evidence: Zero processes belonging to this run work directory after teardown. The device-wide count was 1, which is the operator own runit guest and is reported separately instead of being counted as a failure of this run.

notes: Direction C, C1-C4, on the device with three real boots (fresh, resume, resume). The snapshot is COLD state: the filesystem comes back, RAM does not, and resuming costs a boot -- there is no RAM save/restore in this port. This harness needed three fixes before it could measure anything: it must down the instance before each resume (`up` adopts a live daemon and returns 0 without booting), it must archive the console log instead of deleting it (the daemon holds the handle), and every marker must be base64 in the typed command because the console echoes what it is given.
known_limits_observed: Resume returns the FILESYSTEM only: processes running in the guest do not come back, and the cost is one boot.
Base-image identity is size+mtime by default; the full sha256 is checked only with UML4TERMUX_SNAPSHOT_VERIFY_DIGEST=1 because it reads the whole image.
Gate parity for the boot-path COW policy (reuse vs write) is checked in CI with the cow-ensure hook; this record covers the device behaviour.
